newsitem.title: CANADA: Band-Ore intersects more Timmins gold.
newsitem.headline: Band-Ore intersects more Timmins gold.

text.p: Band-Ore Resources Ltd said on Wednesday that step-out drilling at its Timmins, Ontario gold exploration property intersected the Golden River deformation zone.
Three gold bearing zones were intersected in the step-out hole, with values as high as 0.11 ounces of gold a ton of ore over a minable width, Band-Ore said.
"The company is now confident that the Golden River zone can now be traced continuously for more than four kilometers across the 100 percent owned Thorne property," Band-Ore said.
The Golden River zone on the Thorne property remained open to depth and to the east and west, Band-Ore said.
The company also said that Battle Mountain Gold Co found gold mineralization on Band-Ore's Thunder Creek property next to the Thorne property.
Battle Mountain has an option to earn a 60 percent interest in the property by spending C$1.5 million on exploration.
Battle Mountain's drilling intersected an altered and mineralized gold bearing porphyry with highly anomalous gold values up to .023 ounces of gold per ton over 200 metres, Band-Ore said.
